newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Precious metals seen under pressure.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Precious metals seen under pressure.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold will come under downside pressure on Friday following losses on Comex and could possibly test support at $323.00/$322.00 an ounce, traders and chartists said.
Silver, in line with gold, will probe support at $4.40, while platinum will try to build a base above $425.00, they added.

GOLD - Losses on Comex and a steady dollar are likely to see prices move towards support at $322.00/$323.00 an ounce on Friday. "The move below expected resistance at $325.00 does not bode well for a market which is firmly entrenched in a bear mode," one London trader commented.
The recent failure to overcome resistance at $330.00 has helped to dent gold's technical outlook.
Traders said that they now expected liquidation from producers and investment funds which ultimately could push prices towards $320.00.

Referring to the Comex December gold contract, Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said, "Rumours circulating in the market maintain their bearish tack, with gold set to undergo renewed producer selling as they look to recoup losses of recent months."
Squires said gold was now targeting support initially at $322/21, followed by $315.00.
At 0700 GMT spot gold was quoted at $323.50/324.00, versus Thursday's London close of $325.90/$326.40.
SILVER - The failure to move above resistance at $4.50 and gold's lower stance will see prices under downside pressure. Traders suggest that the market will test support at $4.40 and possibly lower.
"Like gold silver has little in the way of upside potential...it's due for a fall," one trader said.
Squires of Rudolf Wolff, referring to the September Comex contract, pegged support at $4.30 and $4.25, with the longer downside target at $415.00.
At 0700 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.41/4.43, against $4.49/$4.51.
PLATINUM - Improved Russian supplies will keep the market on a downside track, traders said.

"...traders should remember that the Russians effectively control the market at present and supplies will dry up when they feel prices have dropped too low," brokers GNI said in their commodity report.
"This is a floor-finding operation," GNI added.
If prices breach $425.00 traders expect a test of $420.00.
Resistance was placed at $440.00 and $450.00.
At 0710 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $421.00/424.00, compared with $424.50/$427.50.
